scope: Follow-up UI inspection and settings-change notification probe. Internal viewport scale/FSR remain unverified.

ui_inspection.reason: Exited simulation to inspect native editor menus, then closed the isolated Workbench normally before its capture deadline.
observations: UI inspection completed with user permission. Workbench 1.8.0.13.
Read Resource Manager File > Options: General and World Editor tabs. These are editor preferences (FPS cap, autosave, selection outlines, etc.). Cancelled without applying changes.

Read File > Project Settings for the isolated addon: PC configuration, engine default settings, engine settings path EngineUserSettings.conf. Cancelled without applying changes. No main-viewport effective scale/FSR readout was observed.

Returned the isolated World Editor from simulation to edit mode. Read Shading (Lighting, Channels), View (visualizers/gizmos/world bounds), Camera (near/far/FOV/aspect ratio and navigation). No scale/FSR control was observed in those menus.
Exited only the isolated Workbench instance via its close button. The runner recorded natural exit 0 without capture completion; this run is UI inspection evidence, not a capture.
No UI screenshots were saved or published.

notification_probe.operation: After two simulation seconds, set VideoUserSettings.ResolutionScale to 0.25, set FsrEnabled to false and call GetGame().UserSettingsChanged() once. Continue the controlled camera and environment capture. No SaveUserSettings call.

image.measurement: Mean absolute horizontal RGB difference in 8-bit code values, no resizing or alignment. Descriptive only; not an estimator of internal resolution.

notification_probe.visual_review: Forest, terrain and sky remain detailed, without a clear quarter-resolution effect. No image published.
limits: Set calls and notification were requested; this probe does not verify the effective render pipeline state.
